Played this game when I was much younger and was afraid nostalgia was the only reason I thought this game was good. However, starting again, this game not only aged well but has even more amazing story development and gameplay than I remembered. The dialogue is funny, the characters have nice fleshed out personalities and good character development, the gameplay makes it dynamic compared to traditional visual novels, and the difficulty of the cases is just (w)right. Highly recommend it!

PW:AAT is a compilation featuring the first three games of the iconic franchise.

This game is full of twists and turns, funny characters and an amazing soundtrack that really goes hard. The cases in this game really make you think, and will keep you engrossed.

The first 2 games are already good, but the third game (Trials and Tribulations) is such a masterpiece. This allows for hours of gameplay, which is good for people who want to delve more into the Ace Attorney franchise.

The game is well worth the price, especially during sales. Even if you're not into law that much, you will still enjoy what Ace Attorney has to offer.
Amazing game for those who are head over heels for crime and problem-solving. Comes along with an amazing story featuring the legendary attorney Pheonix Wright

I have played this game intermittently for the past 4 years... and OH BOY does it feel good to finally be done. A bit melancholy, as well. All in all, this is a *really* good set of mystery games. The way cases slowly trickle information as you slowly figure not only whodunnit, but howdunnit is in a way that is near euphoric at times. Additionally each of the games end off in a finale tests Phoenix Wright, his ideals as a lawyer, and his deduction abilities in a way that you will never forget. If this game at all sounds like its for you, it is unlikely you will regret it.

If the name doesn't tip you off, i LOVE Ace Attorney. Not much to say other than that, sadly, it's a fantastic trilogy of courtroom drama, featuring a cast of somewhat sillier characters(they're fairly grounded in the first game, but get goofier later on.) than you would normally expect but they're fun to interact with. The puzzles, sometimes they require a bit of knowhow on what the game WANTS you do. You might know a certain piece of evidence fits into the contradiction, for example, but it's not immediately obvious, WHERE you're supposed to present it to. Just another one of Capcom's greatest hits.

Pros

Same content as phone's port
Save anytime
Controller support (with DS4 prompts with slight modification)
Great high quality sprites and musics

Cons

Bad font selection (ew, serif)
No dual screen mode like on phone
Can't separate dub/sub language
No chat history

Recommended when you have big screen and you don't have smartphones. Otherwise, stick to phone's port.

One of my favorite series since the Nintendo DS era. Seeing it remastered with HD graphics and the first three games bundled into one makes it even better. It's a very engaging visual novel with cases that will keep you thinking since it always takes surprising turns. It keeps getting crazier, especially it hits the second game! The lore that spans between all three games is interesting. Being put in the shoes of a lawyer also is a unique premise. The dialogue is very well written with a lot of humor and pretty much every character is memorable. I recently speedran the game to get all achievements and I think it says a lot that I still remembered the whole trilogy after all these years.

The story and characters pull you right into the story, the game is dramatic over the top fun, somewhat like a visual novel that's very interactive and there's a court room element with twists and turns with each new piece of information. Definitely give this original trilogy a try if you're at all interested!

Never played any Phoenix Wright games before and decided to try it with this PC release.
Phoenix Wright is a detective game set in Japan the USA with heavy cultural influences from Japan where you play as a defense lawyer and DESTROY witnesses with FACTS and LOGIC by identifying contradictions in their statements.
Some of the solutions are not that obvious though, meaning a brute force approach with save scumming where you try every combination of statements and evidence may be necessary unless you are willing to spoil yourself searching online for answers.
I also found myself getting stuck a few times searching for clues / evidence in the Investigation parts of the game because I missed one little thing, and the game doesn't give you hints as to what you might have missed and doesn't let you proceed until you find everything.
I also experienced soft locks a few times while playing it so I highly recommended players to keep multiple rotating saves and save often.
All that said, the story is pretty good and all the characters are quirky and interesting. It was worth the pain of playing through just to experience it.

A fantastic mystery/detective visual novel mixed with a courtroom drama.

The collection contains the first three original games from the Nintendo DS, each containing about four to five chapters. The games being "Ace Attorney", "Justice for All", and "Trials and Tribulations". You work your way through court proceedings, attempting to discern fact from fib, uncover evidence from the scene of the crime, question witness testimonies, and most importantly, uncover the truth of what really happened.

The only real complaint I have is that the solutions for some of the puzzles are truly headscratching. A majority of the time, you're not expected to remember any fine details, and anything you do need to know/remember is logged in the Court Record for your convinence. But even then, some of the solutions present in some of the trials felt a little far fetched for my logic. As a result, save scumming until I eventually just brute forced the right answer occured a few times. Thankfully this seemed to be an exception, as for the most part I've been able to make educated guesses to narrow down the possible options. And when you suddenly get a flash of realization, it's one of the biggest dopamine hits you can get.

Peak lawyer (bluffing) simulator. You play as a lawyer named Phoenix Wright who defends his clients by presenting his attorney badge. It is one of the games where you need to use your noggin to complete the trials. Gameplay consists of two parts, the first one is in the courtroom defending your clients, and the second one is after the trial where you investigate crime scenes and talk. Best part about this is that you watch criminals crash out in the courtroom, literally. The game is worth it if you want to try something unique and like to read a lot.
10/10
